Greece reports five Turkish UAVs in 13 Aegean airspace violations

30 October 2026 · Northeastern / central / southeastern Aegean · Greek-reported Turkish UAVs

Greek-authority-reported Turkish UAV airspace violations

Greek military figures reported on 30 October assign 13 national-airspace violations and 11 Athens FIR infringements to five Turkish UAVs in the northeastern, central and southeastern Aegean. The national-airspace assessment and military attribution are those of Greece; precise tracks remain unpublished.

This is one daily regional record, not 13 attacks. Manned-aircraft infringements and two engagements in the mixed daily account are not evidence of UAV armament, weapons engagement or shoot-down. Exact models, payloads and intended targets remain unknown.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
Turkish military attribution and national-airspace assessment are those of Greek authorities. The Greek-Turkish airspace dispute remains relevant.
Investigation / uncertainty
SKAI and ProtoThema report the same daily Greek military figures, not independent observations. The original GEETHA bulletin was not retrieved directly. Exact tracks, times, UAV models, payloads and intended targets remain unknown; the national-airspace assessment and Turkish military attribution are Greek claims. Two reported engagements do not establish UAV weapons engagement.
